mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle on the copied DNA was most worthwhile: the time-strip showed how chromosome copies reach separate nuclei before the cell splits.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle was less clear than the other steps. The goal named the parts, but centrosomes and tubulin were unfamiliar, so I mainly followed the named pairing.

surprise.text: I was surprised that each copied DNA helix contains one old strand and one new strand.

arbitrary.text: The actin-and-myosin pairing followed the goal, but I did not understand from the result exactly how they split the cytoplasm.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: seeing the copied genome separated and then the cell divide made me curious how the cells become different types.
